issue.pro.sd-boot.title: The device may still boot from eMMC after writing the SD image
issue.pro.sd-boot.description: You selected an SD card image. The current firmware has not passed the SD-first boot check, so the device may still start from eMMC after installation. Choose Review repair in the action bar to review the SD-first boot update.
issue.pro.sd-boot.solution:
1. Choose Review repair in the action bar, review the SD-first boot update and confirm.

2. After the update, run checks again and continue installing the selected SD image.

3. Keep the SD card inserted and reboot after installation. The SD card takes priority; without a card, the factory eMMC system starts.
issue.pro.sd-files.title: The OneKVM SD boot files could not be read
issue.pro.sd-files.description: The device is running from eMMC. An inserted card has the OneKVM Pro SD identifier, but its expected boot layout or files could not be read. This does not establish a boot-priority problem.
issue.pro.sd-files.solution:
1. Verify that you downloaded the SD image for this exact model and that its checksum matches.

2. Shut down the device and reflash the complete .img file to the SD card using a card reader. Let the flashing tool finish its verification.

3. Reinsert the card and power on the device. If boot files still cannot be read, try another card or reader.

These checks only provide guidance. They do not format the card, change boot settings, or write firmware.

issue.pro.sd-boot.firmware.title: Enable SD-first boot
issue.pro.sd-boot.firmware.solution:
Choose Review repair in the action bar to review the SD-first boot update. The installer checks the selected image and device, then asks you to review and confirm before updating boot firmware.

The factory system and boot settings are preserved. Continue installing the SD image after the update, and reboot once installation is complete.

risk.internet.title: Internet connections
risk.internet.summary: iptables / ip6tables · Internet IPv4 and IPv6 destinations
risk.internet.targets: Internet IPv4 and IPv6 addresses used by enabled functions and extensions. See each item for its servers. This is an installation permission check; disabling it prevents continuing instead of applying firewall rules.
risk.internet.point.1: Remote services can log the source IP, ports, connection times and traffic patterns. With NAT this is usually the public egress IP, which may reveal an approximate location or link activity.
risk.internet.point.2: Unencrypted traffic may be observed or altered. A permitted LAN DNS server, proxy or gateway may also relay requests to the Internet.
risk.internet.point.3: Network clients and protocol handlers may contain undiscovered vulnerabilities. Malicious traffic could cause service failures or other security effects; this does not assert a confirmed exploit.
risk.download.title: Installer and image downloads
risk.download.summary: onekvm-installer / curl · onekvm.sh, GitHub or chosen mirror
risk.download.targets:
Bootstrap: http(s)://onekvm.sh and github.com/onekvm/onekvm-installer, or ONEKVM_INSTALLER_RELEASE_URL.
Images: https://api.github.com and https://github.com, GitHub release redirects (including release-assets.githubusercontent.com), or the selected HTTP(S) URL. The bootstrap has already run before this page.
risk.download.point.1: Download hosts and redirect destinations can record the source IP, requested files and access times. Their retention and use of those records may be unknown.
risk.download.point.2: HTTP bootstrap or mirror downloads are unencrypted and may be altered in transit. Downloaded scripts run with the privileges used to launch them.
risk.download.point.3: A malicious image or compromised publisher may control the device and read data after installation. A matching checksum alone does not establish that the publisher is trustworthy.
risk.download.point.4: The HTTP client, metadata reader or image parser may have undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious responses or files.
risk.ntp.title: NTP time synchronization
risk.ntp.targets:
Manual or DHCP-provided NTP servers (addresses depend on network configuration), UDP 123.
When none are configured, public fallbacks:
time.cloudflare.com
time.windows.com
time.nist.gov
ntp.nict.jp
time.aws.com
ntp.tencent.com
ntp.aliyun.com
An unreachable configured server does not automatically activate this fallback list.
risk.ntp.point.1: The NTP server sees the source IP, port and request times. A public server usually sees the public egress IP, which can be used to link activity or estimate a location.
risk.ntp.point.2: Ordinary NTP is unencrypted and does not authenticate the server. Forged time responses may affect one-time codes, certificate validation and log timestamps.
risk.ntp.point.3: systemd-timesyncd may have undiscovered protocol-processing vulnerabilities. Malicious responses could cause service failures or other security effects.
risk.ntp.point.4: The provider may retain or correlate connection records; its actual retention and uses may not be verifiable.
risk.dns.title: DNS name resolution
risk.dns.summary: systemd-resolved · DHCP / RA / manually configured resolvers
risk.dns.targets: DHCP, IPv6 RA or manually configured DNS server addresses. Ordinary DNS uses UDP/TCP 53; encrypted configurations use their configured endpoint and port. Public fallback addresses depend on the image and resolver configuration; they are not assumed absent.
risk.dns.point.1: Resolvers can record the source IP, queried domains and times, even when the transport to the resolver is encrypted.
risk.dns.point.2: Unencrypted DNS may be monitored or altered to return incorrect addresses. Encryption and certificate verification for the destination remain separate protections.
risk.dns.point.3: systemd-resolved may have undiscovered response-processing vulnerabilities; malformed responses could cause service failures or other security effects.
risk.dns.point.4: An untrusted DHCP/RA source may supply an untrusted resolver. Resolver logging, retention and onward sharing may be unknown.
risk.discovery.title: Online device discovery
risk.discovery.targets: The browser visits https://find.onekvm.org (or the configured discovery origin) and probes http://<device-IP>/api/discover on the LAN. This setting exposes a discovery endpoint; it does not make the device register with the website.
risk.discovery.point.1: The discovery website sees the browser connection source IP and visit times; its use of those records may be unknown.
risk.discovery.point.2: Anyone able to reach the device discovery endpoint can read its hostname, model, version and LAN IP without signing in. Browser origin checks do not authenticate direct requests.
risk.discovery.point.3: LAN HTTP discovery responses are unencrypted and may be monitored or modified by an attacker on the path.
risk.discovery.point.4: The browser or discovery HTTP handler may have undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious pages, requests or responses.
risk.stun.title: STUN address discovery
risk.stun.summary: onekvm-server / browser WebRTC · Cloudflare and Google STUN
risk.stun.targets:
Default STUN targets:
stun.cloudflare.com:3478
stun.l.google.com:19302
stun1.l.google.com:19302
Custom STUN URLs replace the configured list; an empty configuration currently uses these public defaults. Both the browser and device may send requests.
risk.stun.point.1: STUN servers see the client source IP, mapped port and request times, which may reveal the public egress IP and NAT behavior.
risk.stun.point.2: WebRTC direct peers may learn public IP addresses while candidates are exchanged and connections are established.
risk.stun.point.3: The browser or webrtc-rs STUN implementation may have undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious responses.
risk.stun.point.4: The server provider may retain or correlate request metadata; the actual retention and sharing may be unknown.
risk.turn.title: TURN video relay
risk.turn.summary: onekvm-server / browser WebRTC · configured TURN endpoints
risk.turn.targets: Only configured turn: / turns: URLs, ports and relay endpoints are used. No default TURN server is configured by this installer. Allowing this item does not create a TURN account or server.
risk.turn.point.1: The relay operator can record both peers IP addresses, connection times and traffic volumes. These records may link their activity.
risk.turn.point.2: A relay can delay or interrupt traffic and affect availability. WebRTC media remains encrypted between its endpoints.
risk.turn.point.3: Relay use may incur bandwidth charges. Leaked or shared relay credentials may be abused within their permitted scope.
risk.turn.point.4: The browser or webrtc-rs relay implementation may have undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious server messages.
risk.acme.title: ACME certificates
risk.acme.summary: onekvm-server · Let’s Encrypt / configured DNS verification provider
risk.acme.targets:
Default ACME directory:
https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory
Cloudflare DNS verification additionally accesses:
https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/
Custom ACME directories and DNS verification webhooks use their configured URLs. No request is needed until certificate automation is configured.
risk.acme.point.1: The certificate provider sees the source IP, requested domains and any supplied account email, which may link the device to those domains.
risk.acme.point.2: Domains in publicly trusted certificates normally appear in public Certificate Transparency logs, potentially exposing private naming conventions.
risk.acme.point.3: Leaked DNS verification tokens or webhook credentials may allow changes to DNS records within their authorized scope.
risk.acme.point.4: Certificate and DNS providers may keep or share request records; actual retention and uses may not be verifiable.
risk.acme.point.5: instant-acme, the HTTP/TLS stack or certificate parsers may contain undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious responses.
risk.update.title: System update queries and downloads
risk.update.summary: onekvm-server / ureq · GitHub API and release downloads
risk.update.targets:
https://api.github.com/repos/<machine-update-repository>/releases/latest
https://github.com/<machine-update-repository>/releases/download/...
Release asset redirects, including release-assets.githubusercontent.com. Custom update sources use the selected URL or server.
risk.update.point.1: Update hosts can log the source IP, requested device repository, files and times. Data retention and use may be unknown.
risk.update.point.2: A compromised publisher or signing key may introduce malicious code through a subsequently installed update.
risk.update.point.3: Installing an update replaces system components and can interrupt access; a faulty update may prevent normal operation.
risk.update.point.4: The HTTP client, update metadata reader or installer may contain undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious responses or files.
risk.extensions.title: Extension catalog and package downloads
risk.extensions.summary: onekvm-extension-host / opkg / wget · configured package feeds
risk.extensions.targets:
Preview feeds:
https://pkg-dev.onekvm.org
https://pkg-dev.sgp.onekvm.org
https://pkg-dev.tyo.onekvm.org
Stable feeds:
https://pkg.onekvm.org
https://pkg.sgp.onekvm.org
https://pkg.tyo.onekvm.org
Only the selected image channel and its configured feeds/mirrors apply; custom feeds use their configured URLs.
risk.extensions.point.1: Feed and mirror operators can log the source IP, catalog and package requests, and access times. Their use of these records may be unknown.
risk.extensions.point.2: Installed extensions run code and may read data, use the network or control devices within their granted permissions. A malicious extension may abuse those permissions.
risk.extensions.point.3: Compromised package publishers or trusted signing keys may introduce malicious packages. Adding a source or key expands the publishers being trusted.
risk.extensions.point.4: An extension may contact its own services after installation. Catalog download permission does not control those connections; network virtual media is provided by extensions.
risk.extensions.point.5: The catalog reader, downloader, package parser or extension host may have undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious metadata or files.
risk.mdns.title: mDNS LAN discovery
risk.mdns.targets: LAN multicast: 224.0.0.251:5353 and [ff02::fb]:5353 (UDP). These are link-local multicast groups, not public Internet servers.
risk.mdns.point.1: Other participants on the LAN can observe unencrypted names, addresses, queries and discovery information.
risk.mdns.point.2: mDNS names and responses are not authenticated and may be impersonated; verify the destination identity when connecting.
risk.mdns.point.3: The resolver may have undiscovered multicast packet-processing vulnerabilities triggered by malicious LAN traffic.
risk.cpu.title: Processor use
risk.cpu.summary: Linux kernel · local CPU and associated power circuitry
risk.cpu.targets: The local processor and associated power circuitry. No remote server is inherent to processor use.
risk.cpu.point.1: High-frequency acoustic noise or electromagnetic emissions associated with processor activity and power circuitry may reveal computation information under specific hardware, workload and measurement conditions. Exploitation may require close proximity or specialized sensors; no exploitable leak on this device is confirmed here.
risk.cpu.point.2: The processor, firmware or operating system may contain undiscovered side-channel or isolation vulnerabilities; this notice cannot enumerate all future attack methods.
risk.memory.title: Memory use
risk.memory.summary: Linux kernel · local memory and controller
risk.memory.targets: Local memory, its controller and associated power circuitry. No remote server is inherent to memory use.
risk.memory.point.1: High-frequency electromagnetic or power-circuit noise during memory access may reveal access patterns or information under specific measurement conditions. This does not mean ordinary audible noise exposes all memory data or that a leak on this device has been confirmed.
risk.memory.point.2: Memory hardware, its controller or management software may have undiscovered faults or vulnerabilities that affect data confidentiality or integrity.
risk.storage.title: Storage access
risk.storage.summary: Linux / onekvm-installer · local storage and controller
risk.storage.targets: Local installation storage, its controller and power circuitry. No remote server is inherent to local storage access.
risk.storage.point.1: Acoustic, high-frequency power-circuit or electromagnetic signals during storage activity may reveal access patterns under specific hardware and measurement conditions. Recovering data from such signals is not established for this device.
risk.storage.point.2: Storage firmware, drivers or filesystem software may have undiscovered vulnerabilities affecting data confidentiality, integrity or availability.
risk.linux.title: Linux kernel use
risk.linux.summary: Linux kernel · local system calls, drivers and protocol stacks
risk.linux.software: Linux kernel (process, memory, device and network management)
risk.linux.targets: The local Linux kernel and its system-call, driver and protocol interfaces. Remote addresses depend on the applications and enabled network protocols; see the corresponding items. There is no single remote server inherent to kernel use.
risk.linux.point.1: The kernel runs with high privileges and manages memory, storage and devices. A kernel defect may expose data, bypass isolation or crash the entire system.
risk.linux.point.2: A malicious kernel build or loaded module can execute privileged code and control the device. Only load kernels and modules from trusted publishers.
risk.linux.point.3: System calls, drivers, filesystems and network stacks may contain undiscovered vulnerabilities triggered by malicious processes, devices, files or packets. Actual impact depends on the vulnerability, configuration and exposure; this is not a confirmed flaw on this device.
